analysis.title: International Market Intelligence | Morning Briefing, October 22, 2026
key_insights: Markets are choppy. US tech gains and the EU unwind came after META and TSLA earnings failed to lift AI stocks further. KOSPI is at its lowest level since April.
Positive Russia/Ukraine headlines marginally raised year-end ceasefire odds, which remain low at about 20%. Reports of potential US/Israel strikes after the midterms are circulating.
The Middle East situation is no longer about oil supply because flows have recovered. The pressure now comes from higher shipping costs.
EU equities are rotating into defensives, in line with JPM desk flows. This is driving the widest index dispersion since June.
EU momentum stocks have taken a hit. They broke an 11-day loss streak yesterday, tied for the longest since 2007. Cyclicals are in focus as reporting picks up, and earnings momentum remains strong.
French 10y OAT yields broke 5% for the first time since 2002. JPM futures data show investors continue to add to OATs.
Clients are cautious on tech because of recent volatility, the momentum unwind and earnings risk. JPM's fundamental view is unchanged.

JPM sees three supports for tech. Flows and liquidity positioning metrics are well below the mid-September highs. Neoclouds are not a large segment of the AI ecosystem, and the tech sector runs a financing surplus of about $400bn this year, with debt issuance mostly used to maintain buybacks. Tech ETF flows hit their 2nd highest on record, partly from retail buying the dip.

The NDX vs RTY positioning gap is +3.4z, the widest heading into Mag7 earnings season since 2021. Positioning Intel says the gap's size reveals little about relative performance 1 month or 1 year ahead.
Joyce's takeaways from the 2026 IMF/World Bank meetings: the tone was selectively risk-on, with an emphasis on quality and diversification rather than blanket buying of AI equities.

UK September inflation rose slightly more than expected. Headline CPI was +0.5% m/m and 3.5% y/y, and core was +0.3% m/m (2.8% y/y). JPM raised its inflation profile, with peaks in 1Q27 at 4.6% y/y headline and 3.1% core. It keeps its call for BoE hikes in November and February and sees increased risk of another move in 2Q27.

Tesla is focused on deploying Optimus internally in its own factories, with external commercial shipments targeted for late 2027. JPM's CIIF tour found the most tangible demand among suppliers of sensors, 3D vision, data-collection devices, reducers and dexterous hands, not at the robot OEM level.

JPM is tactically bullish on global equities. It prefers the US and Asia (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan) over the EU. The US is overheating, Europe is recovering from stagflation, and Asia has pockets of both.

A broadening trade can return, more clearly in the US than the EU. Europe's earnings fundamentals are good and positioning gives a buy signal. JPM wants stability in EGB spreads before gaining conviction in EU broadening.

JPM's longs are tech and supercycle themes (inference, semi cap, less-levered hyperscalers, AI-vulnerable software), cyclicals with a secular tailwind (EU and JA banks, EU industrials, JA machinery, GE Infra, EU miners), EU pharma, UKX and selectively the consumer.
JPM's shorts are AI-vulnerable names ex-software, short-cycle data center capex names, EU insurance, challenged industries (autos, chemicals, Asian consumer electronics, medtech) and MDAX.

EM has recovered over 9% of its drawdown since the end-July bottom but is still off YTD highs. JPM is bullish on EM and favors country-relative trades given expected divergence at the country and sector level.
Positioning Intelligence: hedge funds drew down -2.1% MTD globally (from -0.8% last week). APAC lagged most at -3.8% MTD. Multi-strat de-grossing was close to the worst of the past 2 years.

US positioning was around the 40th percentile, yet the backdrop was fragile. Gross exposure was high, flows into tech had been near multi-year highs, and NDX long vs RTY short futures skews were extreme. AI Core Revenue positioning is still 94th percentile (12m) and Utilities are heavily under-owned.

JPM sees the setup as echoing 2023 more than 2018. HFs are about +6% YTD and equities are up about +13% MXWD and +14% SPX, a cushion that historically supports positive 4Q outcomes unless earnings or data deteriorate. It sees a 4Q rally as more likely than not.
